cap.convergent: Oceanic plate sinks beneath a continent. Coral flashes are earthquakes tracing the slab down to ~700 km.
cap.divergent: Plates pull apart; rising magma freezes into new crust and records alternating magnetic stripes.
cap.transform: Plates slide horizontally. Stress builds where the boundary locks, then releases in earthquakes.
cap.normal: Stretching: the hanging wall slides down the fault.
cap.reverse: Compression: the hanging wall is pushed up and over.
cap.strike: Shear: the blocks slide sideways and the road is offset.
cap.P: P wave · ≈ 6 km/s · rock compresses along the direction of travel. Follow the coral particle.
cap.S: S wave · ≈ 3.5 km/s · rock shears at right angles to travel. Follow the coral particle.
cap.R: Rayleigh surface wave · ≈ 3 km/s · the ground rolls in ellipses that fade with depth.
cap.tsunami: Speed = √(g × depth). Watch the wave slow down and grow taller as the sea shallows.

mag.area_note: Circle area = energy released. Each step ≈ 32× more.

depth.omori: Aftershocks per day after a mainshock (Omori’s law)
